solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Highland slopes, west-facing, dry up what’s left of brambles

indicators.note: the left-hand end of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter is kept
in an across entry west is leftwards, so facing west means reading from right to left

blocks.note: the leftmost letter of brambles
to sear is to dry up or scorch

explanation.surface: A forager on a Scottish hillside finds the brambles dried up and picks over what remains.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed SEAR follows the B, so the order of the clue is not the order of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brae is the Scots word for a hillside or steep bank, so the plural names Highland slopes.

clue.text: Roaring tomfoolery about a bar’s closure

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for tomfoolery wraps round the other pieces
a word's closure is its final letter, so only the end of bar is used

blocks.note: tomfoolery is rhyming slang for jewellery, and bling is showy jewellery
taken as written
the last letter of bar

explanation.surface: Someone is laughing loudly at the silly antics as a pub closes for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: Tomfoolery here is not nonsense: in cockney rhyming slang it is jewellery, which leads to BLING; A and the R that ends bar go inside to make BLARING.
explanation.definitionFit: Blaring describes a loud, harsh noise, much like something roaring at full volume.

clue.text: Place of children’s tales off about one word of action, eg

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for off surrounds the other parts

blocks.note: food that is off smells rank
the Roman numeral for one
a verb is a doing word, an example of a word of action

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a classic setting for children's stories has gone off, with talk of action words.
explanation.walkthrough: The riverbank is home to Mole, Ratty and friends in The Wind in the Willows, a classic of English children's literature.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wind in the Willows, a famous children's book, is set largely along a river's edge, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Australian Left blame free estate

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for Australian
L is the abbreviation for left
odium is the disgrace or blame attached to someone

explanation.surface: An Australian politician on the Left avoids blame.
explanation.definitionFit: An alodium is land held outright, with no feudal lord or rent owed, hence an estate held free of obligation.

clue.text: American rigs beginning to haul in shipping order thus held up

indicators.note: to haul something in is to take it inside, so one piece is placed within another
in a down entry, holding something up means reading it from bottom to top
the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the start of haul is used

blocks.note: S.O. is the abbreviation for shipping order
the first letter of haul
so means thus or in this way

explanation.surface: American trucks haul in cargo, with a shipping order on hold.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside SO, then SO turned upside down follows. In American slang to shoo is to fix a race, which is where shoo-in comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang uses shoo for fixing or rigging a race, as in a shoo-in, so shoos means rigs.

clue.text: Dark attempt to cramp women’s cunning

indicators.note: to cramp something is to confine it tightly, so the word for attempt encloses the rest

blocks.note: a shy is a try or throw, as in a coconut shy
W is the abbreviation for women
art means craft or cunning

explanation.surface: A sinister attempt to restrict women's ingenuity.
explanation.walkthrough: Cunning is used in its older sense of skill or craft, not slyness.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarthy describes a dark or dusky complexion, so it serves as a synonym for dark.

clue.text: Astonishing chart that signals caution in place of confinement

blocks.note: slang from surfing and skateboarding: sick means amazing
CH is an abbreviation for chart
the amber traffic light warns drivers to take care

explanation.surface: A striking chart flags a warning about conditions in a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Chart is not a whole word here but its abbreviation CH. Confinement is also the old word for being ill or in childbed, which is why a sickroom fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick chamber is a room where an invalid is kept to bed, so it is literally a place of confinement through illness.

clue.text: West Indians get stuck into these when about to wail mostly

definitions.text: West Indians get stuck into these

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
about means surrounding, so the word for when goes round the shortened word

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
to keen is to wail in grief

explanation.surface: People from the Caribbean throw themselves into a lament.
explanation.walkthrough: KEEN loses its last letter and sits inside AS. Akee (ackee) fruit is a staple of Jamaican cooking, notably ackee and saltfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The akee is a tropical fruit widely eaten in the Caribbean, so the people there tuck into it.

clue.text: What’s necessary is lost rare reward

definitions.note: noun; requite is a rare noun meaning repayment

indicators.note: lost means gone, so the letters of is disappear from the longer word

blocks.note: a requisite is something that is required
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A precious bonus is gone, though it was essential.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IS out of REQUISITE. The word rare belongs to the definition, flagging an unusual sense.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb requite means repay; Chambers also lists it as a rare noun for repayment or recompense.

clue.text: Almost flat, good for local’s basket

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a true surface is flat and level
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A nearly flat basket used by someone from the area.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUE loses its E before G is added. Local signals a regional word: the trug comes from Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: A trug is a shallow wooden garden basket from Sussex, a dialect word used by local people.

clue.text: Once greatly revered drummer in time going north

indicators.note: in a down entry, travelling north means reading upwards, from bottom to top
in places the drummer inside the time word

blocks.note: a day is a period of time
dr is the abbreviation for drummer used in band line-ups and liner notes

explanation.surface: A drummer who was once idolised keeps time as the band heads north.
explanation.walkthrough: Once means the word is archaic: Spenser used ydrad, with the old Y- prefix of past participles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ydrad is a Spenserian past participle of dread, meaning feared or held in awe, an obsolete form for greatly revered.

clue.text: With it missing is Jacobi perhaps back unshaven?

indicators.note: missing means absent, so the letters of it are taken away from with
back means the name is read backwards

blocks.note: with, from which it is removed
taken as written
Sir Derek Jacobi is the English actor

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the actor Jacobi, now back without his trendiness, has grown a beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With it' looks like fashionable, but it is with minus it, leaving WH. Jacobi is a surname here and the wordplay needs his first name, Derek.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiskered means having whiskers or a beard, which is what an unshaven face shows.

clue.text: King’s reps let in small female birds

indicators.note: in tells us the word for let goes inside the other pieces

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
to let a property is to hire it out
a reeve is the female of the ruff, a wading bird

explanation.surface: The monarch's representatives allow a few small hen birds through.
explanation.walkthrough: The reeve, the female ruff, is a dictionary favourite of barred-grid setters. A shire-reeve was the king's officer in a county, and the word later became sheriff.
explanation.definitionFit: Shire-reeves were royal officials who administered counties on the monarch's behalf, the forerunners of sheriffs.

clue.text: Maintain average over week

blocks.note: AV is the abbreviation for average
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
W is the abbreviation for week

explanation.surface: Keep up a steady average across the week.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to assert or declare, as one maintains that something is so.

clue.text: Interrupt food to down quart

indicators.note: to down a drink is to swallow it, so the food word takes the other piece inside

blocks.note: cheer can mean food and drink, as in good cheer
QU is an abbreviation for quart

explanation.surface: Someone breaks off eating to knock back a quart of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Good cheer is the old sense of fare or provisions, which is why food can stand for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To chequer is to vary or break up a pattern, and Chambers lists the sense of interrupting.

clue.text: Active kid with more fish

indicators.note: active means lively and on the move, so the letters are stirred into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of kid and more joined together

explanation.surface: An energetic child asks for more seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: The red moki is a New Zealand sea fish with reddish stripes, one particular kind of fish.

clue.text: Plate out of Endeavour’s introduction, north of Oxford?

indicators.note: an introduction is what comes first, so only the opening letter is taken
in a down entry, being north of something means coming above it, so placed before it

blocks.note: hors is French for out of, familiar from hors de combat
the first letter of Endeavour
an oxford is a type of laced shoe

explanation.surface: A dish from the first episode of Endeavour, the detective drama set in Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Endeavour suggests Inspector Morse, but it only gives its first letter; out of is French HORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Farriers and racing people call a light horseshoe a plate, so plate is a trade synonym for it.

clue.text: Upright character delivers flowers

blocks.note: the letter I stands upright
to deliver someone from a thing is to rid them of it

explanation.surface: An honest person hands over a bunch of blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Irids are plants of the iris family, so the word names a group of flowers.

clue.text: Kept in tower in the main young one’s first to be snatched

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word one
something snatched is grabbed and held, so the fish word takes in the letter

blocks.note: the main is the sea, and a sild is a young herring found there
the first letter of one

explanation.surface: A young child at sea is about to be grabbed and locked away.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is the old word for the open sea, so a young one in the main is a young fish, SILD; O goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A silo is a storage tower for grain, so something silo'd has been stored in such a tower.

clue.text: Refuges from the rain? Kiss and there’s love initially up in the air

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of love is taken
things up in the air are unsettled, so these letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: buss is an old word for a kiss
the letters of there's
the first letter of love

explanation.surface: A couple shelter from a downpour, kissing and dizzily in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Bus shelters are roofed stops where people waiting wait out the weather; the question mark flags this as one example of a refuge.

clue.text: One in sect somehow uses sin

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive in some unspecified way, so they need rearranging

blocks.note: the letters of uses and sin together

explanation.surface: A member of a religious group somehow makes use of sin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Senussi are a Muslim religious order of North Africa, and the word also names an individual follower.

clue.text: English near blooming Spain — let’s go!

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
NR is the abbreviation for near
flowers that are out are in bloom
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: An English tourist, near flowering Spain, urges everyone to set off.
explanation.walkthrough: Blooming is not a mild curse here but describes flowers that are out.
explanation.definitionFit: En route is also used as a command urging departure, a call to get on the way, much like let's go.

clue.text: Strangely sessile plants

indicators.note: strangely says the letters behave oddly, so they must be rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of sessile

explanation.surface: Some plants are oddly stalkless.
explanation.walkthrough: Sessile is a botanical word for a leaf or flower with no stalk, which makes the surface sound like a botany note.
explanation.definitionFit: Seseli is a genus of umbelliferous herbs, related to parsley, so seselis are plants of that kind.

clue.text: Keepers of quarry — as managers we’d come unstuck

indicators.note: to come unstuck is to fall apart, so the letters separate and regroup

blocks.note: the letters of managers and we'd

explanation.surface: Park rangers complain that, as managers, they would fail.
explanation.definitionFit: Game wardens protect wild animals that are hunted, and quarry means hunted animals.

clue.text: I emptied and put back dustbin at a stretch

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, leaving only the outer letters
put back means the remaining letters are written in reverse

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
dustbin with its inside removed

explanation.surface: Someone empties the dustbin and puts it back, a chore lasting ages.
explanation.walkthrough: I looks like the speaker but stands for the number one.
explanation.definitionFit: On end means continuously, as in hours on end, which is what doing something at a stretch means.

clue.text: Old Italian turned up very good mine

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word up means reading it from bottom to top

blocks.note: so means very, as in so good
naval slang calls a depth charge a can, a type of mine; good means effective

explanation.surface: An elderly Italian found an excellent mine.
explanation.walkthrough: Only very is turned up; the can is a depth charge in naval slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscan was an ancient language of southern Italy, and an Oscan was one of its speakers, an Italian of antiquity.

clue.text: Twerps stumped up dollar on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top
in a down entry, on top means placed above, so it comes first

blocks.note: DOL is an abbreviation for dollar
ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: Fools who were baffled paid up a dollar extra.
explanation.walkthrough: Stumped up looks like paid up, but stumped is the cricket dismissal, ST on a scorecard; stumping is when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while the batsman is out of the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp and a dolt are both informal words for a stupid person.

clue.text: Counties wanting hard breeds

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing from the counties word

blocks.note: the shires are the English counties
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: Rural districts short of tough stock-breeders.
explanation.walkthrough: Breeds is a verb here, as in a stallion siring foals.
explanation.definitionFit: To sire is to father offspring, so it is a verb synonym for breeds.

clue.text: Special charity do giving support for miners

blocks.note: SP is an abbreviation for special
a rag is a student fundraising event for charity, as in rag week

explanation.surface: A special fundraising event is held to help mineworkers.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag week is a British student tradition of stunts and events raising money for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprag is a prop or strut used to hold up coal in a mine, literally a physical support for miners.

clue.text: Flipping wife departs big house

indicators.note: flipping something over in a down entry turns it upside down

blocks.note: a wife is jokingly called a rib, after Eve made from Adam's rib
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: An exasperated husband says his wife is leaving their mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: Flipping looks like a mild oath, but it is the turnaround signal. Big house is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird is British slang for prison or a prison sentence, and the big house is slang for prison too.

clue.text: Bishop accepting eccentricity got up to parley dully

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the bishop abbreviation holds the next letter inside

blocks.note: BP is the abbreviation for bishop
e is the mathematical symbol for eccentricity
rose means got up

explanation.surface: A quirky bishop stood up to drone on in negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccentricity is not oddness but the e of conic sections in geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: To beprose is to talk about something in prose, at tedious length, hence talking without spark.

clue.text: This month’s church is Latin, close to the Vatican City

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter of the word that follows is kept

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Latin
the final letter of the
V is the international vehicle code for Vatican City

explanation.surface: This month's church service is in Latin, near the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: This month points to the time of year the puzzle ran: Chislev falls around November and December.
explanation.definitionFit: Chislev (Kislev) is the ninth month of the Jewish calendar, which the puzzle's publication date fell in.

clue.text: Furniture left centre backwards

indicators.note: backwards means the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
the hub is the centre of something

explanation.surface: Furniture has been left in the middle, back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Buhl is inlaid work of brass and tortoiseshell, and also furniture decorated in that style.

clue.text: Blow blasted Starmer on the back of sloth

indicators.note: blasted means blown apart, so the name's letters are scattered and rebuilt
on the back of means following, so the sloth word comes first

blocks.note: the ai is the three-toed sloth
the letters of the surname Starmer

explanation.surface: Keir Starmer, the UK Labour leader, is blasted for his slowness.
explanation.walkthrough: Starmer looks like the politician but is just seven letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow is a gust of wind, and an airstream is a moving current of air.

clue.text: With light receding around district we enjoy nature

definitions.note: a clause spoken by the answer: the solution is a plural noun, the people who say this

indicators.note: something receding moves backwards, so the word is read in reverse
around means surrounding, so the reversed word encloses the district abbreviation

blocks.note: the sun is the source of daylight
DIST is an abbreviation for district

explanation.surface: As daylight fades across the area, people declare their love of the outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is what nudists might say, with nature hinting at being in the natural state, naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudists practise naturism, so they are people who enjoy nature in the sense of going unclothed.

clue.text: No more favours for some local victories

blocks.note: first meaning: an obsolete word for goodwill or favour
second meaning: a Scots word for prizes or victories

explanation.walkthrough: No more marks the first sense as obsolete; local marks the second as dialect, Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Gree was once a word for goodwill or favour, and in Scots it means a prize or the first place in a contest.
